subject: AeroNova order form: pricing ladder, minimum commit evidence & Net-45 exception
messages:
From: AeroNova Procurement <procurement@aeronova.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Choi <emma.choi@aeronova.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: RFQ / PO attached — pricing ladder questions and Net-45 ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — AeroNova is excited to move forward. Attached is our draft PO for the pilot (AeroNova_PO_202803.pdf). Before we get procurement to issue the PO I need to confirm a few commercial details on the Order Form:

- Pricing ladder: the draft shows three tiers (0-50k / 50-200k / 200k+ monthly). Do these thresholds map to committed spend per month or to billed usage?
- Minimum commit evidence: our finance team needs a short checklist of what constitutes proof that we hit an annual minimum to trigger slab pricing (invoices, usage reports, signed acceptance).
- Net terms: AeroNova normally uses Net-45. We understand Redwood’s standard is Net-30; is there flexibility for Net-45 for this account?
- Invoicing: we want to split invoicing across two legal entities due to local tax jurisdiction — is that supported, and what evidence do you need for entity mapping?

Can you send a short note addressing the above and any example language we should expect in the Order Form (MSA references welcome)? We’d like to keep the procurement cycle moving this week if possible.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Senior Procurement Manager | AeroNova Systems
procurement@aeronova.com

Attachment: AeroNova_PO_202803.pdf (PDF, 78KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: AeroNova Procurement <procurement@aeronova.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFQ / PO attached — pricing ladder questions and Net-45 ask

Sara — thanks, and congrats on moving this to procurement. Short answers up front, with next steps below: 

1) Pricing ladder: thresholds are evaluated on billed usage per calendar month. Slab pricing applies to all usage in any month where billed usage crosses the relevant threshold. We can add a clarifying clause in Appendix B (Order Form pricing schedule) to make this explicit.

2) Minimum commit evidence: typical acceptable evidence is (a) monthly invoices showing usage billed by Redwood, (b) monthly usage reports from our billing portal, or (c) an executed amendment signed by both parties acknowledging the committed shortfall. We'll include this list in the Order Form appendix.

3) Net terms: Net-45 is not standard for our self-serve tiers but for committed order forms we can make an exception with Finance sign-off. That usually requires: (i) PO on file referencing the Order Form, (ii) credit check / references (light), and (iii) an agreed prepay or activation milestone (often 10% up front) if Net-45 is requested.

4) Multi-entity invoicing: supported but requires entity mapping (legal name, tax id, remit-to address). We'll need a signed schedule that maps invoice amounts to entity: simple two-row table in the Order Form works.

Proposed next step: Kimberly on our side will draft a redline of the Order Form showing the pricing ladder language and a Net-45 carveout with the milestone. Kimberly — can you take the draft and produce a redline for AeroNova? Karthik, can you flag any billing/ops constraints?

I’ll confirm the timeline to procurement once we have the redline.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Thanks Kimberly — the redline looks reasonable. A few clarifying items from Legal/Tax before we sign:

- VAT / sales tax handling: AeroNova operates in two jurisdictions (US and EU). We need to confirm whether Redwood will issue VAT invoices or whether AeroNova must self-account. Please confirm invoicing VAT fields that will appear on the invoice (VAT number, tax amount by line).
- Tax residency evidence: please confirm the list of documents Redwood requires to accept the entity mapping (e.g., certificate of tax residency, W-8/W-9 as applicable). We can provide the certificate once we have the required field list.
- DocuSign: please send the clean Order Form + DocuSign link to legal@aeronova.com and cc procurement.

We are okay proceeding with Net-45 if Redwood confirms VAT handling and provides the tax evidence checklist. Otherwise procurement will default to Net-30 and we’ll sign.

Best,
Daniel Park
Corporate Counsel | AeroNova Systems

Daniel / Sara — thanks for the quick review. Confirming next steps and what we will provide today: 

1) VAT / tax handling: Redwood will include VAT fields on invoices. For EU-related charges we can issue VAT invoices where applicable; for US-only charges we’ll include tax lines where required. Kimberly copied Schedule X to capture the legal name + tax id per entity.

2) Tax residency evidence checklist (what we need from AeroNova):
   - Certificate of tax residency for each non-US entity (PDF)
   - W-9 for any US entity or W-8BEN-E for non-US entities that claim treaty benefits
   - Legal entity name + registered address + remit-to bank details (for PO mapping)

We will accept a single consolidated PDF containing the residency certs + W-8/W-9. The attached placeholder (tax_residency_certificate_AeroNova.pdf) is just a stub note for procurement; please replace with the official docs.

3) DocuSign: Kimberly will send the clean Order Form and DocuSign link once we receive the entity mapping and residency docs. If AeroNova can provide the residency docs today we can route to Finance and finish approvals for Net-45 (assuming the 10% activation prepay transacts).

Action items:
- AeroNova: send tax residency + W-8/W-9 and confirm which entity receives the activation prepay.
- Redwood (Kimberly + Karthik): prep clean Order Form + DocuSign after we receive the above.

We’ll keep the PO on file and block a DocuSign window for Monday. Thanks all.

Best,
